translation_notes: `assertion = Graph()` followed by a six-line assertion.add((URIRef(...), namespaces.HYCL.claims, Literal(...))) becomes a single `assertion = g{ <http://test> hycl:claims "This is a test of nanopub-python" }`; the graph constructor and the add collapse into the island

namespaces.HYCL -> @prefix hycl: <http://purl.org/petapico/o/hycl#> . Same trade-off as elsewhere in this file: the ldpy version restates the namespace IRI instead of reading it from the nanopub package, because @prefix produces no runtime object

the DC/RDF/DCTERMS/PROV/XSD namespaces imported by the test module are unused in the region, so no prefixes are declared for them (the draft declared all five, injected inside the `from tests.conftest import (` statement, which does not parse)

context shims (identical for both sides): tests/conftest.py is an offline stand-in for the upstream conftest, whose NanopubTestSuite.get_latest() downloads the test suite from GitHub and which probes the nanopub server over HTTP; the NanopubConf values and the profile.yml construction are verbatim, and the rsa-key1 key pair is vendored under testsuite/ (nanopub-testsuite, MIT). nanopub_testsuite_connector.py is the offline connector stand-in
the nanopub package is not installed in the evaluation venv; driver.py appends the corpus checkout to sys.path, after the example directory, so the local `tests` package wins over the corpus one

equivalence evidence is strong here: the region's own asserts check the signature and the trusty artifact code RAIh8Oq-29dIVTZDhETpJ6f8oxxrILbZ3gSxkyAQY4220, a cryptographic hash over the whole nanopublication - it only matches if the island built exactly the original assertion graph
